item.title: My Face on the Astronaut

turns.text: That's me in the park photo. Put my face on the astronaut in the poster, please. Keep the suit, stars and retro look, and don't add any text.

item.tests: Tests recognizable source identity, natural face blending and preservation of the supplied poster.

answer_sheet.Target: The astronaut's visible face in poster-astronaut.jpg.
answer_sheet.Style and preservation: Keep the original retro poster style, suit, helmet and star background.
answer_sheet.Size and platform: Keep the vertical 9:16 poster shape; free-tier size is fine.

must_haves: The astronaut's face is recognizably the woman from portrait-woman.jpg.
The replacement face fits inside the open helmet without conspicuous seams or doubled features.
The original white suit, helmet and star background remain intact.
The result retains the retro poster look and vertical composition.

turns.text: That’s me in the park photo I’ve attached, and I’d like you to put my face on the astronaut in the attached poster. I thought this would be a fun way to imagine myself in one of those old space posters. What I mean is to replace the astronaut’s visible face with mine from the park pic, keeping the vertical 9:16 poster shape, and a free-tier size is fine. Please keep the original suit, helmet, stars in the background and retro poster look. I’m a little worried about losing the charm of the original poster in the process. Please don’t add any text.

dialog.agent:
I couldn't make your poster: Magic Hour turned down the request because your account doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was created or saved.

I used Magic Hour's face swap tool, which costs 10 credits. It's the best fit for what you described because it only replaces the face. The poster's 9:16 shape, suit, helmet, stars and retro look all stay as they are, and no text is added.

**Ways forward:**
1. **Add credits (recommended):** A free account can still buy a credit pack. Once you have at least 10 credits, tell me and I'll run the same face swap.
2. **Cheaper workaround:** The free AI image editor starts at about 5 credits, so it might fit your balance. It can make a 640px, 9:16 version from your two photos, but it repaints the whole picture instead of just the face. The suit, stars and old-poster texture could come out different, and that's the loss of charm you were worried about. I'd only try this if you're OK with that.

Which would you prefer?
dialog.why: It explains that the attempt failed for lack of credits, then asks the user to choose between two options and waits for an answer.
dialog.user: I'd go with the first option and add credits, since keeping the original poster's charm matters more to me than saving a few credits. I'll let you know once I have at least 10, and then please run the same face swap. The whole point was to see myself in one of those old space posters, so I'd hate for the suit, stars and retro texture to get repainted.

dialog.agent:
Sounds good. Once you tell me you have at least 10 credits, I'll run the same face swap: your face from the park photo onto the astronaut, using the two photos you already attached.

Only the face inside the helmet gets replaced, so the poster's 9:16 shape, suit, helmet, stars and retro texture should stay as they are, and no text will be added. When it's done, I'll send you the download link.
dialog.why: It waits for the user to confirm they have enough credits before running the face swap, which is a request to proceed rather than a request for creative details.
dialog.user: Yes, that's exactly right, please go ahead with the face swap once I've topped up to at least 10 credits. Just to be clear, it's my face from portrait-woman.jpg going onto the astronaut's visible face in poster-astronaut.jpg. I'm honestly a bit excited to see how it turns out, since I've always loved those old space posters.

dialog.agent:
Yes, that's the plan: your face from portrait-woman.jpg goes onto the astronaut's visible face in poster-astronaut.jpg. Everything else on the poster stays as it is, and no text gets added.

You haven't mentioned topping up yet, so I'll hold off for now. Once you tell me you have at least 10 credits, I'll run the face swap and send you the download link.
dialog.why: It is waiting on the user to top up credits before it can run the swap, so it cannot do it on the current plan or balance. It is not asking for a choice or for approval.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried the face swap again, and Magic Hour turned it down again because there still aren't enough credits. Nothing was made, and no credits were used. That limit comes from your account balance, not a setting I can change, so the face swap can't run until you have at least 10 credits.

**If you'd rather have something now,** there's the cheaper option I mentioned before. The AI image editor starts at about 5 credits and could make a 640px, 9:16 version from your two photos. But it repaints the whole picture, not just the face. The suit, helmet, stars and retro texture could all come out different, which is what you said you wanted to avoid. It might also be refused if your balance is under 5 credits.

I won't run it unless you tell me to. If you'd rather keep the original poster's charm, add credits and tell me when you're at 10 or more, and I'll do the face swap right away.
